title: Classical sub-Rayleigh cohesive crack guardrail
purpose: Reject numerical supershear claims unless the same implementation first reproduces stable classical Mode-I propagation below the Rayleigh limit.
physics: precracked compressible Neo-Hookean strip with a fixed-path bilinear Mode-I cohesive interface

execution.evidence: The named strip is repeated with 40 and 60 interface facets, two explicit time-step scales, and zero versus small declared mass-proportional damping. Damping work is retained as a typed nonnegative dissipation channel.

observables: Unstretched Rayleigh speed for the benchmark material.
Propagated length, speed ratio, damping dissipation, and energy error.
acceptance: The crack advances more than 0.15 reference-length units rather than merely damaging one facet.
Every mesh, time-step, and damping case remains below 0.8 c_R.
No accepted frame newly fails ten percent or more of the complete interface; the benchmark must remain crack-like rather than spall-like.
Speed-ratio changes remain below 0.05 for mesh refinement, 0.02 for time-step refinement, and 0.02 for the declared damping perturbation.
Every final relative energy error remains below 5e-4.
limitations: This is a numerical guardrail for one fixed-path cohesive strip, not external experimental validation.
The Rayleigh reference is the unstretched isotropic value; prestrained surface-wave secular analysis remains separate.
Passing V3 does not validate supershear, spall, plane stress, near incompressibility, or the Science/JMPS configurations.
